item.content:encoded:
News / TradingView / XAUUSD: Gold Reclaims $4,000 as Fed Week Begins. Silver Sinks to 2026 Lows

XAUUSD: Gold Reclaims $4,000 as Fed Week Begins. Silver Sinks to 2026 Lows 2 min read

XAUUSD Key points: Gold prices cross back above $4,000 Fed week to define market sentiment Silver languishes at a 2026 bottom

Bullion rebounds after its worst week since June as softer oil prices offer relief. 📈 Buyers return after a difficult week Spot gold XAUUSD recovered about 0.4% to $4,010 an ounce early Monday, reclaiming the $4,000 threshold after initially trading below it. The rebound follows a roughly 4% weekly decline, gold’s steepest since June. Friday’s selling took bullion to its lowest level since mid-July. Silver also recovered, rising 0.6% to $54.15, but still hovering at a low not seen since November 2025. Its outlook has an additional complication: industrial demand makes it sensitive to economic growth alongside interest rates and investment flows. 🏦 Oil and interest rates shape the outlook Softer oil prices provided some breathing room. Brent retreated toward $115 following reports of Qatari mediation efforts in Tehran, although ongoing attacks in Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns alive. An energy shock can raise both defensive demand and inflation expectations in the gold market, leaving the anticipated central-bank response especially important. The Fed is widely expected to hold rates Wednesday, while traders assigned a 75% probability to a December increase in the latest snapshot. Gold pays no interest, so expectations of higher borrowing costs can increase the appeal of interest-bearing alternatives and restrain bullion even during periods of geopolitical uncertainty. 🤑 Dollar’s impact on gold Lower Treasury yields and a softer dollar offered counterweights. The US 10-year yield traded near 4.97%, while the dollar index eased toward 101.64. Dollar weakness can make bullion less expensive for overseas buyers, but a lasting recovery also depends on how yields and inflation expectations evolve together. Thursday brings another major test after the Fed announcement. September PCE inflation and the first estimate of third-quarter US GDP arrive at 8:30 a.m. ET. Economists expect core PCE inflation around 3.1% annually. 📊 Holding $4,000 becomes the immediate challenge Friday’s low near $3,975 is the nearest clearly observed downside reference. Holding above it would preserve the possibility of a recovery, while a sustained break beneath it would extend the recent sequence of losses. Lower prices are attracting some physical buyers. Reuters reported stronger Indian purchases during the Dussehra festival last week, while Chinese demand remained steady despite cautious jewelry spending. That offers a source of underlying support, although this week’s immediate direction is likely to depend heavily on policy guidance, yields and the dollar.
